# NLP for Cybersecurity / NLP per la sicurezza dei sistemi cyber fisici - Theresa Master Course

## Master Program
THERESA - digiTal tecHnologiEs foR thE Security of criticAl infrastructures

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP), starting with the fundamentals and progressing to cutting-edge techniques like Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will learn about text preprocessing, vectorization, and traditional NLP tasks such as text classification and named entity recognition. The course then delves into deep learning methods, including RNNs, LSTMs, and the Transformer architecture, and how they're applied in NLP. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with building and fine-tuning NLP models, as well as responsible AI practices. By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of both classical and modern NLP techniques and be able to apply them to real-world problems.

## Textbook

Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft) by Dan Jurafsky and James H. Martin [https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/)

## Topics

### 1. NLP Fundamentals (16 hours)

*   **Introduction to NLP:** Definition, key challenges, and real-world applications.
*   **Text Preprocessing:** Tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, stop word removal, and handling special characters.
*   **N-gram Language Models:** Understanding and implementing N-gram models for text prediction.
*   **Text Classification using Naive Bayes:** Building probabilistic classifiers for text categorization.
*   **Text Vectorization Techniques:**
    *   Bag of Words (BoW)
    *   TF-IDF
    *   Word Embeddings (Word2Vec, GloVe, fastText)
*   **Neural Networks for NLP:** Introduction to artificial neural networks for text processing.
*   **Transformers:** Understanding the attention mechanism and Transformer architecture for modern NLP.

### 2. Large Language Models (24 hours)

*   **Introduction to AI and LLMs:** Overview of Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models.
*   **Prompt Engineering:** Crafting effective prompts for various tasks and optimizing LLM performance.
*   **Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG):** Combining LLMs with external knowledge sources for enhanced responses.
*   **AI Business Applications:** Practical applications of LLMs in business contexts.
*   **Agentic AI:** Building AI agents that can autonomously perform tasks using tools.
*   **LLM Evaluation:** Metrics and methods for evaluating LLM performance (accuracy, fluency, hallucinations, etc.).
*   **Tools for LLM Development:** Development frameworks and tools for building LLM applications.
*   **NLP for Critical Infrastructure Design and Cybersecurity:** Applying NLP techniques to secure cyber-physical systems.

### 3. Practical Applications (8 hours)

*   **Hands-on Implementation:** Practical sessions implementing NLP and LLM techniques.
*   **Real-world Projects:** Applying learned concepts to cybersecurity and critical infrastructure scenarios.
*   **Tool Integration:** Working with vector databases, RAG systems, and LLM frameworks.

## Assessment Criteria

*   Final Pass/Fail Exam OR Project OR paper presentation
